text: Scales measuring motor function are crucial to objectively document changes in functional ability in people with neuromuscular diseases [ 1 – 4 ]. They are widely used in clinical practice to monitor disease progression and adapt rehabilitation interventions. In clinical trials, functional scales are not only used to track progression but also to quantify treatment efficacy, stratify patients, and support regulatory approval, which explains their increasing importance with the development of genetic and pharmaceutical treatments for diseases such as Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) and Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) [ 5 , 6 ].
source_label: Barriers and levers to using an app for motor function assessment by therapists in hospitals: A qualitative study of the MFM-Play app
